newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill Shi'ite Moslem activist in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill Shi'ite Moslem activist in Pakistan.

text.p: Gunmen shot dead a Shi'ite Moslem activist and wounded two of his companions in the city of Multan, in Pakistan's central province of Punjab, on Saturday, police and hospital sources said.

The gunmen, their faces masked by scarves, fired on three local leaders of the Shi'ite Tehrik-i-Jafria Pakistan group with Kalashnikov assault rifles, killing one and badly wounding the others, the sources said.
The three Shi'ites were attacked after they had attended a marriage ceremony in the city's Lal Shah district.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the killing, which appeared to be the latest in a vendetta between rival Sunni and Shi'ite Moslem groups in Pakistan.
At least seven people have been killed in the feud in southern Punjab in the past 12 days.
Shi'ite activists have in the past blamed such attacks on the militant Sunni Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan group.
Sunni-Shi'ite disputes over religious doctrine have often spilled into violence in Pakistan, where Shi'ites make up about 15 percent of the predominantly Sunni population.
